UnitStatement: ADR document titles follow the form 'ADR-NNNN: <short decision title>'.
An ADR records a Status field with allowed values: proposed, accepted, superseded by ADR-NNNN, or rejected.
An ADR records a Date field giving the date of the status shown, formatted YYYY-MM-DD.
An accepted or rejected ADR requires a cited human authority: who ruled in role terms, the date, and where the ruling is recorded.
Without a cited human ruling, the decision stays proposed and the choice remains TBD.
An ADR records a Decision log cross-reference to a DEC-NNN row in execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md section 12, or TBD.
The Context section states what problem or fork forced a decision.
In Context, state facts with their sources and label anything unverified as ASSUMPTION or TBD.
Context must record what the status quo bought (why it existed) as well as why it is insufficient.
The Decision section states the decision so an implementation agent can act on it without reinterpreting.
Record only what was actually ruled; downstream details that remain open stay TBD in Decision and route to the human-ruling queue.
The Alternatives Considered section lists each option that was on the table with the reason it was rejected or deferred.
An accepted decision with no recorded alternatives is suspect.
The Consequences section records what the decision costs and changes: new prerequisites, build/test posture changes, performance or size impacts, and new obligations on later work.
Consequences must include negative consequences; an ADR with only benefits is incomplete.
The Affected Packages section lists which packages or deliverables the decision touches, per the decomposition in execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md.
The Reconsideration Triggers section states concrete conditions under which the decision must be re-opened and routed back to human ruling.
Every accepted decision must list at least one reconsideration trigger.
The Source References section lists documents, rulings, code locations, and registers that the ADR's claims trace to.
ADRs record software development decisions only.
ADRs are not release-readiness, professional-approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or engineering-code-compliance claims.
ADRs must stay code-neutral (no protected standards text, tables, formulas, or proprietary values) per docs/CONTRACT.md.
